_comment: Copy to config.local.json and fill in. config.local.json is gitignored; keep real phone numbers out of every other file.

poll._comment: Apps are event-driven (NSWorkspace) and are not polled at all. Browser tabs must be polled; 10s measured at ~0.9% of one core.

_matching: Site rules match the domain AND all its subdomains. 'reddit.com' also catches old.reddit.com and m.reddit.com. Services owning more than one domain (x.com/twitter.com, youtube.com/youtu.be) need each listed separately.

transcription._comment: 'alternate' strictly ping-pongs between passages across unlocks. 'random' picks one each time.
transcription._comment_normalize: Gutenberg text uses curly quotes and em dashes; normalization means a straight ' or -- still matches.

notify._comment_contacts: Put real handles here, e.g. "+15551234567" or an Apple ID email. This file is gitignored.
notify.message: Heads up: I just turned off Friction, my distraction blocker. It re-arms in an hour.
notify._comment_confirmation: 'manual' shows you the sent message and requires you to confirm you saw it land. Delivery cannot be verified programmatically without Full Disk Access.

browsers._comment: Firefox does not expose tabs to AppleScript, so it is blocked as an application (see tier3.apps) rather than swept.

_manual_locks: When YOU lock something by hand outside its scheduled hours, the unlock terms change: apps come back with no timer at all (you did the work, it's yours until you re-lock it or 06:00 arms it), and sites come back for manual_unlock_minutes. mode 'choice' lets you pick timed or untimed at unlock time; 'always_timed' always puts you on the clock.

global_switch._comment: One switch locking every app and site at once. Locking is free; unlocking costs a confirmation plus the transcription. Its unlock releases ONLY this lock -- schedule locks and per-item locks still apply, so it cannot be used to bypass the tiers.

_switches: whole_tier_switch gives a tier a lock-all/unlock-all row. Only tier 1 has one; tiers 2 and 3 are per-item on purpose, so one challenge cannot open the whole tier.
_grouping: A site entry can be a single domain, or a list of domains for one service reached by several names (x.com and twitter.com). A group locks and unlocks as one thing. The FIRST domain is the key, so adding an alias to an existing entry does not void unlocks already recorded against it.
